summary: Snohomish County, WA DNR tower built in 1961 to watch Spada Lake logging; Glory served 1961-63; windstorm in 1962; gone by 1966; remains scattered downslope.

facts.design: 12-foot wooden DNR live-in tower (FFLOS and Firelookout); temporary 12-foot tower with a small trailer for the observer (WillhiteWeb); one observer described it as 8 feet
facts.status_note: Windstorm in October 1962 took the roof and then the tower (WillhiteWeb); FFLOS and Forest Lookouts say gone by 1966. Scattered remains reported downslope.

staffing.status: Glory (surname unknown) was the lookout 1961 to 1963, per WillhiteWeb; she may have continued a few years longer

access.note: Reached on foot across DNR land from Culmback Dam, Spada Lake; the county road is gated for winter at Olney Pass. Snohomish County PUD describes its Spada Lake recreation sites as open year-round for day use. No agency statement on the lookout site itself was found.

visit.trail_note: Park at Culmback Dam if the Olney Pass gate is open, then hike about 2.5 miles with about 1,000 feet of climb, partly on old roads and a steep dozer trail (WillhiteWeb).

events.note: Temporary 12-foot wooden DNR tower with a small live-in trailer, built to watch logging and dam building for Spada Reservoir
Glory (surname unknown) is the only named observer; per WillhiteWeb she served 1961 to 1963

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS, Firelookout and Forest Lookouts give 12 feet. WillhiteWeb says one observer described it as 8 feet and suggests the difference may be the shorter tower she saw. Not resolved; the record and story show 12 feet with the 8-foot account noted.

WillhiteWeb dates the windstorm that took the tower to October 11, 1962, and says the lookout was gone by 1966. FFLOS, Firelookout and Forest Lookouts date only its being gone to 1966. Both are kept; the 1962 date is the windstorm and 1966 is the date recorded as gone.
FFLOS gives 2,560 ft (780 m) and Firelookout gives 2,560 ft. WillhiteWeb gives 2,500 ft. The record's 780.3 m matches FFLOS and is kept.

notes_for_editor: Record matches sources on agency, county, 1961 build and registration; the record's 780.3 m elevation matches FFLOS. Sources conflict on height (12 vs 8 ft) and on the loss date (1962 windstorm vs gone by 1966); both kept. Observer Glory's surname is not in any source. Access rests on WillhiteWeb's route and the PUD recreation page; no agency statement on the lookout site was found. The WTA trip report is dated 2024-05-23 by its URL. No photos with image URLs were read.
